Q1: The chemical 1,2-Dichloro-1,1,2,3,3-pentafluoropropane largely exhibits a data-deficient hazard profile (Tier 4) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), inhalation (IHL), oral (ORL), dermal and eye (SKN), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN). However, it is categorized as having a demonstrated low/moderate hazard (Tier 3) for endocrine disruption (EDC).
Q2: This chemical is identified on the EPA PFAS 2024 list, indicating it meets the structural definition of a Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substance (PFAS), a class of chemicals subject to reporting due to environmental and health concerns. It is not currently designated on any lists as a low hazard chemical.
Q3: 1,2-Dichloro-1,1,2,3,3-pentafluoropropane is poorly characterized, with only 26 scientific literature references—significantly below the median for our dataset of similar chemicals. This lack of study is further indicated by six out of seven hazard classes being data deficient (Tier 4), though its molecular formula is well-defined and it is not classified as an incompletely characterized substance.
